node-1.label: A woman in her 70s had a pruritic and painful periorbital eruption lasting 1 month

node-2.label: Patient is a woman in her 70s with a 1-month history of pruritic and painful periorbital eruption

node-3.label: Medical history included lupus nephritis requiring hemodialysis, immune thrombocytopenia, acute myeloid leukemia, chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy, deep vein thrombosis, diverticulitis, and postcolectomy diarrhea

node-4.label: Past treatments included hydroxychloroquine, which resulted in retinal toxic effects, and lenalidomide, which severely worsened platelet count with a nadir of 28 ×10^3/μL

node-5.label: Physical examination demonstrated scaly, crusted pink plaques involving the periorbital skin

attrs.why: The pathologist and the laboratory physician now independently and explicitly favor an autoimmune/inflammatory process, with the pathologist specifically calling it lupus-related on the basis of vacuolar interface dermatitis with follicular involvement and epidermal atrophy sampled from the affected left periorbital eyelid lesion; the patient's lupus nephritis and immune thrombocytopenia further reinforce this category. The missing DIF, ANA/anti-dsDNA/anti-Ro/anti-La, C3/C4, tissue microbiology, and precise medication timeline limit definitive lupus confirmation rather than the broader autoimmune/inflammatory classification. Confidence remains 0.80.

The new biopsy finding of vacuolar interface dermatitis with follicular involvement and epidermal atrophy is characteristic of an autoimmune/interface process rather than an infectious dermatosis, and the pathologist explicitly favors autoimmune over infection. Although tissue microbiology/PCR has not yet been performed, the morphology does not support infection. Confidence decreased from 0.25 to 0.08.

The biopsy shows an interface dermatitis pattern that the pathologist attributes to an autoimmune process rather than a drug reaction, and the previously implicated agents (hydroxychloroquine, lenalidomide) are historical rather than current exposures, with prior lenalidomide clearly worsening platelets (arguing against a current drug eruption). Confidence slightly reduced from 0.10 to 0.07.

The biopsy demonstrates vacuolar interface dermatitis with follicular involvement and epidermal atrophy rather than atypical cells or neoplastic infiltration, and the pathologist explicitly ranks neoplasm below autoimmune/inflammatory rash. This new histologic evidence argues against neoplastic skin infiltration. Confidence decreased from 0.10 to 0.05.

Because DIF was not performed and ANA/anti-dsDNA/anti-Ro/SSA/anti-La/SSB and C3/C4 were not performed/reported, definitive confirmation remains limited, so confidence stays at 0.60, below the 0.80 of the broader autoimmune/inflammatory category.
